customSections.text:
The Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR), Outpatient Endovascular and Interventional Society (OEIS), and Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) issued a joint evidence-based letter in 2022 specifically addressing insurer denials of peripheral atherectomy.

Key points from the joint statement:
- Peripheral atherectomy is a covered, evidence-based treatment for symptomatic PAD supported by Level A/B evidence from multiple prospective trials (DEFINITIVE LE, LIBERTY 360, CONFIRM registries)
- Atherectomy as vessel preparation prior to DCB or stenting is clinically appropriate and reduces the need for stenting in calcified lesions
- ISR is a well-established indication for atherectomy; repeat stenting in ISR is associated with worse outcomes
- Blanket coverage denials for atherectomy are inconsistent with the published evidence base and societal guidelines
- The joint statement is available for inclusion in prior authorization requests and appeal letters

Reference: SIR/OEIS/SCAI Joint Evidence-Based Letter on Peripheral Atherectomy Coverage, 2022. Available at sir.org, oeis.org, and scai.org.

# Peripheral Atherectomy — Authorization Guide

_CPT Codes · ICD-10 · Payer Requirements_

(Back link: /atherectomy)

## CPT Codes

| CPT Code | Description | Device Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 37225 | Revascularization, endovascular, open or percutaneous, femoral, popliteal artery(s), unilateral; with atherectomy, includes angioplasty within the same vessel, when performed | Any |
| 37227 | Revascularization, endovascular, open or percutaneous, femoral, popliteal artery(s), unilateral; with transluminal stent placement(s) and atherectomy, includes angioplasty within the same vessel, when performed | Any |
| 37229 | Revascularization, endovascular, open or percutaneous, tibial, peroneal artery, unilateral; with atherectomy, includes angioplasty within the same vessel, when performed | Any |
| 37231 | Revascularization, endovascular, open or percutaneous, tibial, peroneal artery, unilateral; with transluminal stent placement(s) and atherectomy, includes angioplasty within the same vessel, when performed | Any |
| 37221 | Revascularization, endovascular, open or percutaneous, iliac artery, unilateral; with atherectomy, includes angioplasty within the same vessel, when performed | Any |
| 37223 | Revascularization, endovascular, open or percutaneous, iliac artery, unilateral; with transluminal stent placement(s) and atherectomy, includes angioplasty within the same vessel, when performed | Any |
| 37232 | Revascularization, endovascular, open or percutaneous, tibial/peroneal artery, each additional vessel; with atherectomy (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure) | Add-on |
| 37234 | Revascularization, endovascular, open or percutaneous, tibial/peroneal artery, each additional vessel; with transluminal stent placement(s) and atherectomy (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure) | Add-on |

_Note: Atherectomy CPT codes include angioplasty within the same vessel. Do not separately bill angioplasty (37224, 37228, 37230) when atherectomy is performed in the same vessel._

## Covered ICD-10 Diagnoses

| ICD-10 | Description | Rutherford |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I70.211 | Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with intermittent claudication, right leg | 2–3 |
| I70.212 | Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with intermittent claudication, left leg | 2–3 |
| I70.221 | Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with rest pain, right leg | 4 |
| I70.222 | Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with rest pain, left leg | 4 |
| I70.231 | Atherosclerosis of native arteries of right leg with ulceration of thigh | 5 |
| I70.241 | Atherosclerosis of native arteries of right leg with ulceration of heel and midfoot | 5 |
| I70.261 | Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with gangrene, right leg | 6 |
| I70.262 | Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with gangrene, left leg | 6 |
| I70.291 | Other atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities, right leg | 1–3 |
| I70.292 | Other atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities, left leg | 1–3 |
| I70.311 | Atherosclerosis of unspecified type of bypass graft(s) of the extremities with intermittent claudication, right leg | 2–3 |
| I70.411 | Atherosclerosis of autologous vein bypass graft(s) of the extremities with intermittent claudication, right leg | 2–3 |

## Payer-Specific Requirements

### CMS / Medicare (LCD L35041 — Peripheral Vascular Disease)

**Covered Indications:**
- Symptomatic PAD (Rutherford 2–6) with hemodynamically significant stenosis (>50%) confirmed by duplex ultrasound, CTA, MRA, or angiography
- Critical limb ischemia (Rutherford 4–6) — strongest indication; limb salvage intent
- In-stent restenosis of peripheral vessels
- Calcified lesions where atherectomy facilitates balloon or stent delivery

**Non-Covered / Limitations:**
- Asymptomatic PAD (Rutherford 0)
- Mild claudication (Rutherford 1) without failed conservative therapy
- Atherectomy billed separately from angioplasty in the same vessel (bundled per CPT rules)

**Documentation Requirements:**
- ABI and/or duplex ultrasound confirming hemodynamically significant disease
- Rutherford classification documented in procedure note
- Failure or contraindication to supervised exercise therapy (claudication)
- Wound care documentation for CLI/tissue loss cases

### BlueCross BlueShield
- Covered for Rutherford 3–6 with angiographic confirmation of >50% stenosis
- Rutherford 2: requires documentation of failure of supervised exercise therapy ≥3 months and optimized medical therapy
- Prior authorization required for elective (claudication) cases; CLI cases may be expedited
- Peer-to-peer review available and recommended for complex TASC C/D lesions
- SIR/OEIS/SCAI 2022 joint statement accepted as supporting evidence

### Aetna
- Covered for CLI (Rutherford 4–6) and moderate-to-severe claudication (Rutherford 3) with hemodynamically significant disease
- Atherectomy as vessel preparation for DCB: covered when calcification grade is moderate-severe or ISR is present
- Requires documentation: ABI, duplex or angiographic imaging, Rutherford classification, wound documentation if applicable
- Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin #0282: Peripheral Atherectomy — updated 2023

### Cigna
- Covered for symptomatic PAD (Rutherford 2–6) with >50% stenosis confirmed by imaging
- Rutherford 2–3: requires failure of 3-month supervised exercise program and optimized antiplatelet/statin therapy
- ISR: covered without additional conservative therapy requirement
- Calcified lesions: atherectomy as vessel preparation covered when calcification is documented on fluoroscopy or IVUS
- Prior authorization required; clinical notes, ABI, and imaging must be submitted

### UnitedHealthcare
- Covered for CLI (Rutherford 4–6) without additional requirements
- Claudication (Rutherford 2–3): requires ABI <0.8, failure of supervised exercise ≥3 months, and optimized medical therapy
- UHC Medical Policy: Endovascular Procedures for Peripheral Arterial Disease (updated 2024)
- Peer-to-peer review strongly recommended for TASC C/D lesions in claudicants
- SIR/OEIS/SCAI 2022 evidence-based letter referenced in UHC policy as supporting documentation

## SIR / OEIS / SCAI 2022 Joint Evidence-Based Statement

The Society of Interventional Radiology (SIR), Outpatient Endovascular and Interventional Society (OEIS), and Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) issued a joint evidence-based letter in 2022 specifically addressing insurer denials of peripheral atherectomy.

Key points from the joint statement:
- Peripheral atherectomy is a covered, evidence-based treatment for symptomatic PAD supported by Level A/B evidence from multiple prospective trials (DEFINITIVE LE, LIBERTY 360, CONFIRM registries)
- Atherectomy as vessel preparation prior to DCB or stenting is clinically appropriate and reduces the need for stenting in calcified lesions
- ISR is a well-established indication for atherectomy; repeat stenting in ISR is associated with worse outcomes
- Blanket coverage denials for atherectomy are inconsistent with the published evidence base and societal guidelines
- The joint statement is available for inclusion in prior authorization requests and appeal letters

_Reference: SIR/OEIS/SCAI Joint Evidence-Based Letter on Peripheral Atherectomy Coverage, 2022. Available at sir.org, oeis.org, and scai.org._
